q: 1. Cohesion less soils are formed due to
options: leaching action of water on rocks
blowing of hot and cold wind
explain: Cohesionless soils like sand and gravel are primarily formed through the physical/mechanical disintegration of rocks.

q: 2. Thixotropy of soils refers to ...........
options: gain of strength with time after remoulding
loss of strength with time after remoulding
thickening of soil with particles with water
explain: Thixotropy is the property of some clays to regain a portion of their lost strength over time at a constant water content after being disturbed.

q: 3. Which of the following is responsible for shear resistance in soils?
options: cohesion and adhesion between the soil particles
explain: Based on Mohr-Coulomb theory, shear strength ($s$) comes from two components: internal friction ($\phi$) between grains and cohesion ($c$) between particles.

q: 4. The maximum shear stress occurs on the filament which makes an angle with the horizontal plane equal to ............
explain: In Mohr's circle analysis, the maximum shear stress occurs on a plane oriented at $45^\circ$ to the principal planes.

q: 5. Vane shear test is used for ...............
options: measuring shear strength of cohesive soil
measuring void ratio of sandy soils
explain: The Vane Shear Test is a rapid field or lab method to determine the undrained shear strength of cohesive (clayey) soils.

q: 6. Shearing strength of cohesion less soil depends upon ...............
explain: According to the Mohr-Coulomb criteria, for cohesionless soil (c=0), the shear strength s = σ tan φ, meaning it depends directly on the normal stress (σ).

q: 7. The effective angle of internal friction will be ...............
explain: For most practical soil conditions, the effective angle of internal friction (φ') rarely exceeds 45 degrees, even for very dense sands.

q: 8. In Mohr's stress circle, the co-ordinates of the centre of the circle are ...............
explain: The center of Mohr's circle lies on the normal stress (σ) axis at the average value of the major and minor principal stresses.

q: 9. The angle made by the failure envelope with horizontal in the Mohr's circle gives ...............
explain: The slope of the Mohr-Coulomb failure envelope represents the angle of internal friction (φ), while the intercept represents cohesion (c).

q: 10. Unconfined compression test is generally done on saturated clays for which the apparent angle of shearing resistance is ...............
explain: In an undrained test on saturated clay, the soil behaves as if φ = 0 because the water takes all the initial load.

q: 11. Unconfined compression strength is obtained from ...............
explain: The UCC test is a rapid test where no drainage is allowed, making it a specific type of unconsolidated-undrained (UU) test.

q: 12. The angle between the two planes on which the shearing stress is zero is ...............
explain: Planes with zero shear stress are principal planes, and by definition, the major and minor principal planes are perpendicular (90°) to each other.

q: 13. In Mohr's circle the angle made by the plane which consists of maximum shear stress with horizontal at origin of planes is ...............
explain: Maximum shear stress occurs on planes at 45° to the principal planes.

q: 14. The maximum shear stress in case of Mohr's circle will be numerically equal to ...............
explain: The radius of the Mohr circle represents the maximum shear stress, which is calculated as half the difference between principal stresses.

q: 15. The shear stresses on two planes which are at right angles to each other are ...............
options: numerically equal and of the same sign
numerically equal and are of the opposite sign
explain: To maintain equilibrium, complementary shear stresses on perpendicular planes must be equal in magnitude but opposite in rotational direction (sign).

q: 16. In a strain-controlled shear test ...............
options: the shear force is increases at a given rate
the shearing strain increases at a given rate
explain: In strain-controlled tests, the displacement (strain) is applied at a constant rate, and the resulting resistance (stress) is measured.

q: 17. In a stress-controlled shear test ...............
options: the shear force is increased at a constant rate
the shearing strain increases at a given rate
explain: In stress-controlled tests, the load (stress) is applied in increments or at a constant rate, and the resulting deformation is measured.

q: 18. The stress-strain characteristics will be better observed in ...............
explain: Strain-controlled tests allow for the observation of post-peak behavior (softening), which is difficult to capture in stress-controlled tests.

q: 19. The test which represents the field conditions more closely is ...............
explain: Field loading (like a building) usually involves a constant application of load/stress rather than a constant rate of movement.

q: 20. The value Nφ = tan²(45 + φ/2) is called ...............
explain: Nφ is known as the flow value or the passive earth pressure coefficient for a soil with friction angle φ.

q: 21. Shear strength of soil is determined by the equation ...............
explain: This is the standard Coulomb equation for shear strength where s is strength, C is cohesion, and σ is normal stress.

q: 22. Drainage conditions during test can be controlled best in ...............
explain: The triaxial test allows precise control and measurement of pore water pressure and drainage through the use of valves and a rubber membrane.

q: 23. The type of test in which no significant volume changes are expected is ...............
explain: In a UU test, no water is allowed to leave or enter, so for a saturated soil, the volume remains constant during the test.

q: 24. The type of shearing test in which there is a pre-determined failure plane ...............
explain: In a direct shear test, the soil is forced to fail along the horizontal plane where the two halves of the shear box meet.

q: 25. In a consolidated drained test on a normally consolidated clayey soils, the volume of the soil during the shearing will ...............
explain: Normally consolidated clays tend to contract during shear in a drained test, resulting in a decrease in volume as pore water is expelled.

q: 26. In unconfined compression test, around stresses ...............
explain: The 'unconfined' part of the test name refers to the fact that the lateral (confining) stress is zero (σ₃ = 0).

q: 27. For saturated clays under undrained conditions ...............
explain: Undrained shear strength S (or Cu) is equal to half the unconfined compressive strength qu.

q: 28. The application of deviator stress on a specimen in case of a triaxial test will produce shear stress on ...............
explain: Deviator stress produces shear stresses on all planes except the principal planes (which are the horizontal and vertical planes in this setup).

q: 29. The test that will be preferred for testing of shear strength of a saturated clay is ...............
explain: For soft, saturated clays, the vane shear test is often preferred because it avoids the high disturbance caused by sampling.

q: 30. The line joining the points of maximum shear stresses as the load is changing is called ...............
explain: A stress path is a graphical representation of the locus of stress points (usually the top of the Mohr circle) as the stress state of the soil changes.

q: 31. The coordinates of a point on the stress path are ...............
explain: In p-q space, the coordinates are p = (σ₁+σ₃)/2 and q = (σ₁-σ₃)/2.

q: 32. Most of the shear tests are done in equipment which are ...............
explain: Strain-controlled machines are most common because they allow the test to continue past the peak stress to observe the residual strength.

q: 33. Terzaghi has suggested mobilized cohesion and mobilized angle of internal friction for ...............
explain: To account for the reduced strength mobilized during local shear failure, Terzaghi used reduced values Cm = 2/3 C and tanφm = 2/3 tanφ.

q: 34. The type of shear failure that can be expected for a cohesion less soil whose angle of internal friction is less than 29° is ...............
explain: Empirical guidelines state that local shear failure typically occurs when φ < 29°.
